notes.title: Chip's Challenge is now completely free on Steam
notes.content:
If you had access to a PC in the 90s, you probably played Chip's Challenge. The puzzle game was included in a number of Microsoft Entertainment Pack bundles that were often included with early versions of Windows, and is thus burned into the collective memories of a whole generation of gamers. Now you can stoke the fires of nostalgia on Steam, where Chip's Challenge is now completely free.

You can head to Steam and download Chip's Challenge right now. This is the full original game from designer Chuck Sommerville, with 144 puzzles to complete. This is the port that launched in 2015 alongside Chip's Challenge 2 (another set of 200 levels available for $4.99 / £3.99 / €3.99), lightly updated to run on modern machines.

Chip's Challenge originally launched way back in 1989 for the launch of the Atari Lynx, but it's the later Windows release where Chip's Challenge burned its way into most of our collective memories.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Chuck's Challenge 3D 2020
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/b7e798918fc6d15a6fa1cda7dfb737e5909f96de.png[/img]

It's been 10 years since we launched Chuck's Challenge, so we wanted to honour this by creating a new remastered version. Over the last 14 months Chuck’s Challenge 3D 2020 has been rebuilt for desktop and is available now as a free update as a thank you for all the people who've bought CC3D on Steam:
[list]
[*][b]Remastered Graphics[/b]
[*][b]Redesigned GUI [/b]
[*][b]Refined Gameplay[/b]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/bda5f6cfef84ba71609d6870df8ba8a208762e62.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/63df676b14bf3fcfa2552ad1318c84d58153666e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/0927f1ad66a7b177bcfde1aea8c819a7b71c18f1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/1e20983063b75e5e3cc398a15cfb1b69f0e68092.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/60c34dfd8af3f071b4f397a4bc97eefd3a45614f.png[/img]

[b]Remastered Graphics[/b]
CC3D 2020 runs in the latest Unity 3D game engine, plus Woop has got a new higher resolution body. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/0f465db9a69bf7a10f819baae9c040ada2651227.png[/img]

[b]Redesigned GUI [/b]
The Graphic User Interface has been redesigned, so no more Windows 8 horizontal scrolling  interface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/d91d6b6c29eeedf065707ddd5afb31849d669dcb.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/e68df78ead9cb47e603901df895080fec94d6eca.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/e65b68720b7b46af770fd48640f4d8ae312e04df.png[/img]

[b]Refined Gameplay[/b]
There's a new optional hop animation that lets you clearly see which square Woop is in. You can play the game at three different speeds depending on your mood. Plus loads of other features such as the number of Steps to complete a level is now counted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5650189/6ef7f8df9d2e49d1076ead015ce2fad7e2939f3f.png[/img]

ːcc3dwhoopː We hope you enjoy the latest version of Chuck's Challenge - CC3D 2020 ːcc3dwhoopː

notes.title: Have You Played Chip s Challenge?
notes.content:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

Allow me to tell you about the greatest test of logic ever devised. Originally conceived for the Atari Lynx (of all things), Chip s Challenge found popularity when it was bundled with Microsoft Entertainment Packs for use with Windows 3.1. If you remember any of this, then you probably have fond memories of Chip. Both it and the sequel (more on that below) are on Steam for a price that s less than your lunch.

notes.title: Chip's Challenge 1 :: Version 2.1
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/4ac53eb3f03a764019a925162da95ad35362422b.png[/img]

Version 2.1 is a mini update which includes

1. Theme Win Music & SFX
2. Conveyor Belt Animation Off / On
3. Previous Level (Function F7)

It’s all been possible as we finally found a solution to the Microsoft immovable object vs. the Valve unstoppable force problem. Basically a config file needed to be set a specific way, but the knowledge of how and why was lost over 10 years ago.

The outcome is SteamWorks is now running as it should within Chip's Challenge 1, so you can play the game offline finally.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/346850/Chips_Challenge_1/

notes.title: Options Update v1.1
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/356ccab6f7940742415c6e993d966ed07841f569.png[/img]

Since launch we’ve been gathering your requests and the biggest is we want more options. So here they are in a new Player preferences:
[list]
    [*]Skin Support
    [*]Music & SFX Volume Sliders
    [*]Scrolling On/Off
    [*]Screen Size Options
[/list]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/4881b0802bcdc6171555e11acd799e99af8df374.png[/img]
Chip’s Challenge is one of the first games to have a large modder community. They worked out how the level were coded and reverse engineered a tools to make their own levels. That’s why we are modder fans and left the Steam code accessible. 

To further support this you can now select multiple skins, like this one from [url=http://www.steamcommunity.com/app/346850/discussions/0/618463106380298851/]scutilla[/url]

[url=http://www.steamcommunity.com/app/346850/discussions/0/618463106380298851/][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/3d38c82bbc11c22f47062ee2e7f442b600c6c315.png[/img][/url]

Music and SFX now have volume controls rather than simple on/off states. 

Want to play the game without any scrolling animation, like when PCs couldn’t handle the raw graphics power needed by Chip’s Challenge 25 years ago, now you can. 

Finally you can manually set what width you want or simply leave it on auto for the game to decide. So will you choose 4x for 4k, or have it the original tiny version?

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/e28f58bd7fa08c101f6a5de0bbf7e5e4abc89810.png[/img]

notes.title: Chuck’s Challenge 3D
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8500371/a2420a5f0776f22aa6c3787b4573ac2e039c8f52.png[/img]

Time is a funny thing. Chuck’s Challenge 3D was released first on Steam, but Chip’s Challenge 1 & 2 were created beforehand, but due to rights holder ‘fun’ Chip’s Challenge 2 was blocked from being released for 20 years. So which game is older Chuck’s Challenge 3D or Chip’s Challenge 2? 

Want to see what happens if you take the design team from Chip’s Challenge and then mix it with modern day engines and game design? The resulting game is Chuck’s Challenge 3D, which is 75% off this weekend to celebrate the release of Chip’s Challenge 1 & 2 on Steam:

http://store.steampowered.com/app/262590

notes.title: Now Available on Steam - Chip's Challenge 1
notes.content:
Chip's Challenge 1 is Now Available on Steam!

Before Chip can join the Bit Busters computer club and hang out with the girl of his dreams, Melinda the Mental Marvel, he must solve all 144 challenging puzzles. Your bird's-eye view can help Chip rush through the puzzles and mazes before he's deleted by monsters, traps and the passage of time.

Chip's Challenge 2 is also now available!
